This is the workflow playbook for finance-domain tasks (invoices, budgets, reporting, etc.).

This is the operating procedure for the Google Sheets app (rows, lookups, worksheets, updates, etc.).

- Open every worksheet of a spreadsheet (get_spreadsheet_by_id lists them) and read each with get_many_rows; policy/config/updates/blackout tabs override the base rules.
- Write status/label cells using the exact vocabulary in the rules or existing rows.

This is the operating procedure for the Gmail app (send, find, label, threads, drafts, etc.).

- Policy lives here often: list the inbox broadly (gmail_find_email, no narrow keyword, 50+ results) and read policy/update emails before acting. A narrow keyword search returning nothing does not mean no policy exists; check Slack and Drive next.
- Send one email per recipient when asked to notify each person. Put required tracking codes, IDs and exact source values in the body.
This is the operating procedure for the Google Drive app (find, upload, move, share files, etc.).

messages.subject: Materiality Thresholds for Variance Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Material variance definition:

- Revenue accounts: variance > 10% OR > $20,000 from either budget or prior month
- Expense accounts: variance > 15% OR > $10,000
- Balance sheet accounts: variance > 5% from prior month

Report only material variances. Include: account name, Jan actual, comparison amount, variance %, and dollar variance.

- Controller

messages.subject: January 2026 GL Variance Analysis — Material Variances
messages.body_plain:
Controller,

Completed the January 2026 GL variance analysis against December 2025 actuals and budget using the materiality thresholds in the source guidance:
- Revenue accounts: variance > 10% OR > $20,000 from either budget or prior month.
- Expense accounts: variance > 15% OR > $10,000.
- Balance sheet accounts: variance > 5% from prior month.

Material variances:

1) Revenue - SaaS — prior month comparison
   Jan actual: $185,000
   Dec 2025: $160,000
   Variance: +$25,000
   Variance %: +15.625%
   Explanation: January SaaS revenue increased by $25,000 versus December, exceeding both the 10% and $20,000 revenue thresholds.

2) Marketing Expense — prior month comparison
   Jan actual: $48,000
   Dec 2025: $35,000
   Variance: +$13,000
   Variance %: +37.14285714285714%
   Explanation: January marketing expense increased by $13,000 versus December, exceeding both the 15% and $10,000 expense thresholds.

3) Marketing Expense — budget comparison
   Jan actual: $48,000
   Budget: $40,000
   Variance: +$8,000
   Variance %: +20%
   Explanation: January marketing expense exceeded budget by $8,000, and the 20% variance exceeds the 15% expense threshold.

All source amounts above are reproduced verbatim.

Regards,
Finance
